title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Doji high guards bulls as Fed bets bite
body: The AUD/USD ended the day in the green but finished the week 0.45% lower amid growing bets that the Fed will raise rates next week, boosting the US Dollar. Nevertheless, on Friday, the pair traded at 0.7171, up a decent 0.38%.

title: Oil Rally Pauses on Mideast Diplomatic Efforts
body: Crude oil halted its recent rally on Friday, stabilizing around $100 a barrel after Iranian state media reported that Tehran would hold talks with Gulf states in Oman on the management of the Strait of Hormuz. Diplomats from the Gulf Cooperation Council are scheduled to meet their Iranian counterpart on Monday to explore a possible temporary arrangement for overseeing shipping traffic through the strategic waterway. Adding to the downward pressure on prices, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) raised its forecast for US crude production in 2027 to 14.3 million barrels per day, while the International Energy Agency (IEA) sharply lowered its outlook for global oil demand, projecting a contraction of 2.5 million barrels per day in 2026. In the meantime, China is on track to import roughly the same volume of crude in September as it did in August, with buying recovering from June's decade-low levels. Saudi Arabia has shut its East–West crude pipeline as a precaution following multiple attacks, and Iran-backed Houthi forces have reportedly advanced toward Yemen's Perim Island. Despite Friday's pause, oil prices surged 9.7% over the week. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Ibovespa Falls as Political Risks Persist
body: The Ibovespa slipped 0.6% on Friday, closing at 187,207 points, as the ongoing crisis involving Brazil's Supreme Federal Court continued to stoke political uncertainty and cloud the country's economic outlook. Chief Justice Edson Fachin ordered Justice André Mendonça to lift, within 24 hours, the confidentiality on proceedings related to investigations into Banco Master. The probe includes alleged irregularities in the financing of the film "Dark Horse," a case that could undermine Flávio Bolsonaro's electoral prospects. Investors generally regard Bolsonaro as more fiscally conservative, but concerns over political risk are intensifying just as high domestic interest rates and subdued business activity continue to pressure growth expectations. State-controlled financial stocks retreated, with Banco do Brasil down 1.4%, BB Seguridade off 4.1%, and Caixa losing 2.4%. The utilities sector also weakened, with Axia declining 1.6%. CSN tumbled 7.4% as investors took profits after recent gains, though the stock still ended the week up 4.2% following a change in the company's CEO. Despite Friday's pullback, the Ibovespa advanced 1.1% over the week. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: TSX Gains as Oil Rally Pauses
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index rose 0.5% to close at 35,697 on Friday, as oil prices retreated on signs of potential diplomatic progress in easing tensions around the Strait of Hormuz. Gulf foreign ministers are scheduled to meet their Iranian counterpart in Oman on Monday as part of efforts to build support for a temporary framework to manage shipping through the strait. The pullback in crude prices provided some relief to equity markets. Credit-sensitive financials advanced, with TD Bank and BMO each gaining 0.8%, while Scotiabank rose 0.9%. A rebound in gold prices bolstered heavyweight miners: Agnico Eagle climbed 2.2%, and both WPM and Franco-Nevada added 2.4%. Technology shares also strengthened, mirroring gains in major US hyperscalers and chipmakers. Shopify rose 1.9%, Constellation Software gained 2.5%, and Celestica jumped 6.6%. Descartes Systems surged 6.9% after posting second-quarter revenue that came in slightly ahead of expectations. Despite Friday's advance, the S&P/TSX Composite Index finished the week down 1.7%. title: Wall Street Ends Four-Day Losing Streak
body: US stock indices finished higher on Friday, snapping a four-session losing streak as the recent surge in oil prices and Treasury yields took a breather. The S&P 500 rose 0.9%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 509 points, and the Nasdaq Composite advanced 0.9%. Long-dated Treasury yields retreated from multi-year highs, while fuel prices paused after this week's sharp rally, which had been driven by escalating tensions and reciprocal strikes between the US and Iran in the Persian Gulf. The jump in energy prices had been expected to exacerbate already elevated inflation pressures—headline inflation stood at 3.4% in August—bolstering expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates on Wednesday. Credit-sensitive and growth-oriented sectors benefited from the pullback in oil and yields. Alphabet climbed 1.8%, Amazon gained 1.9%, and JPMorgan rose 0.8%. Oracle, however, reversed earlier strength to close down 1.8% despite posting strong earnings results. Chipmakers were broadly higher, with AMD up 2.5% and Intel advancing 2.6%. Dell Technologies jumped 11.9% to a record high after RBC initiated coverage with an "Outperform" rating. For the week, the major averages still finished lower: the S&P 500 slipped 0.6%, the Nasdaq declined 0.7%, and the Dow lost 426 points.
